scope: every sense authored in tick 4 (shard 13), drawn complete rather than sampled
authoring: parallel family-author agents, one per family, Opus 5 at xhigh, rubric verbatim from .claude/agents/family-author.md
reading: rubric verbatim from .claude/agents/census-reader.md - comparable to census 006

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Cool and quantitative - a measured shortfall below the amount or degree required, with none of the verdict *wanting* carries.

entries.definition: lacking the requisite qualities or resources to meet a task
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flat general word for falling short of what a task demands, registering the shortfall without turning it on whoever bears it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the unmet requirement down to capacity - not that the standard was missed but that it could not be reached.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The harshest here, reading a missed requirement as a verdict on fitness rather than a measurement of it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plainest of these, naming the missing amount outright and stopping there.

entries.definition: inadequate in number of workers or assistants etc.
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Informal, and it carries the strain of working a job with too few hands rather than the bare count.
examples: they're rather short-handed at the moment

entries.definition: inadequate in number of workers or assistants etc.
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: States the shortfall as a plain condition of the staff on hand, neither excusing it nor blaming anyone for it.

entries.definition: inadequate in number of workers or assistants etc.
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Measures the people present against the strength the work was meant to have, framing the gap as a post held by too few.

entries.definition: inadequate in number of workers or assistants etc.
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The flattest of the four - a headcount below requirement, without the felt pressure of *short-handed*.

entries.definition: lacking the requisite qualities or resources to meet a task
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Weighs what is brought against what the task takes and finds the two mismatched, where *inadequate* names the shortfall as a defect in the thing itself.
examples: she was unequal to the task

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The gentlest way of saying the requirement went unmet, setting the demand beside the resource and leaving the failure unassigned where *incompetent* pins it.
examples: unequal to the demands put upon him

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and weighted, as though the amount had been tested against a standard and pronounced short, where *lacking* only reports the gap.

entries.definition: expressing yourself easily or characterized by clear expressive language
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Plain approval of clear, easy expression - it credits a speaker with getting the thought out whole, without *eloquent*'s claim on beauty.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The strongest praise in the family - expression so ready and effective that the manner of it is admired alongside the matter.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: A cool compliment: it names the effortlessness of the speaking and stops there, where *eloquent* reaches for admiration.
examples: able to dazzle with his facile tongue

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praise for speech that runs without a catch in it - flow, where *eloquent* claims power.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The figure spelled out at full length, praise with a flourish that plain *fluent* never attempts.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Figurative and frankly ornamental - it admires the sound of the speaking, where *articulate* admires only its clarity.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approving of the delivery itself - words that arrive without friction - and plainer in register than *eloquent*.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The bare fact of having speech at all, carrying none of the approval that *articulate* does.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely descriptive and formal: it records the capacity to speak and passes no verdict on how well.

entries.definition: speaking or spoken fittingly or pleasingly
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approves speech that fits the occasion and pleases the ear, judging fitness as much as skill, where *fluent* asks only that the words come easily.
examples: a few well-spoken words on civic pride

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Idiomatic and comparatively mild - it frames the disagreement as two things standing opposed rather than as either one being wrong.
examples: the figures are at odds with our findings

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the two sides in active collision, stronger than *at odds* but stopping short of claiming they cannot both stand.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The hardest of the disagreement words - it says the two cancel each other, so one of them has to go.
examples: contradictory attributes of unjust justice and loving vindictiveness

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and measuring - it registers the mismatch against the facts coolly, where *incompatible* pronounces on it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: States the mismatch as a settled property of the thing rather than an observation about it, blunter and more final than *discrepant*.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain, unemphatic name for the fault - it marks a failure to hold together without saying how sharp the clash is.
examples: inconsistent statements cannot both be true at the same time

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and slighting - it allows the thing no smooth stretch at all, where *spotty* at least grants good patches between the bad.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Turns the clash inward so no second party is needed - the thing defeats itself, which is the more damning charge.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and deflating - it breaks the thing into good patches and bad ones, so the complaint carries a grudging concession inside it.
examples: the golfer hit the ball well but his putting was spotty

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Technical and unblaming - it records only that two things fail to correspond and leaves the fault unassigned.
examples: a description unconformable to previous accounts

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The mildest of these - it registers variation without deciding that any part of the thing has failed.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Points at work left undone rather than at a defect - the clash simply stands, not declared unresolvable as *incompatible* would have it.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Absolute where *destroyed* is elastic - it admits no remnant and no degree, and its sweep makes the ruin sound total rather than merely thorough.

entries.definition: affected by blight; anything that mars or prevents growth or prosperity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Ruin as a slow affliction rather than an event - what it marks is not smashed but stopped, held back from growing or prospering again.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Nothingness reached by covering over: the thing is effaced rather than smashed, which makes this the visual member beside the formal *obliterated*.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Financial ruin in the bluntest available word - a single snap rather than a decline, and it reports the loss without blaming the one it fell on.
examples: the broken fortunes of the family

entries.definition: destroyed or badly damaged by fire
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Says the fire went to its end from the inside and left a hollow behind - more final than plain *burned*, and short of gone.

entries.definition: destroyed or badly damaged by fire
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The particle puts the fire's passage across the thing: it names what the flames swept and left behind them, not what they consumed.
examples: a burned-over site in the forest

entries.definition: destroyed or badly damaged by fire
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Reaches from scorched to gone, fixing fire as the cause while leaving open how much survives - which the compounds beside it refuse to leave open.
examples: a burned-over site in the forest

entries.definition: destroyed or badly damaged by fire
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The clipped twin of *burned-out*, its tighter shape making the hollowness sound like the thing's condition now rather than the fire's doing.
examples: barricaded the street with burnt-out cars

entries.definition: destroyed or badly damaged by fire
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The clipped form, and the shorter shape makes it read as a property the thing now has rather than a report of what happened to it, as *burned* does.
examples: a charred bit of burnt wood
barricaded the street with burnt-out cars

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The elastic member: it stretches from merely spoiled to flattened, so it fixes that ruin happened without fixing how much is left, where *annihilated* leaves nothing to measure.
examples: Alzheimer's is responsible for her destroyed mind

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Carries a purpose *annihilated* does not: the completeness is somebody's work, and the word frames what it names as a thing that was to be got rid of.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The formal word for that same ruin: it names the poverty left behind rather than the break itself, so it sounds like a settled condition where *broken* sounds like a moment.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The bare adjectival form states the finished nothingness flatly, without the backward glance at whatever caused it that *obliterated* keeps.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and cold next to *blotted out*: the participle points back at an act, and what is left is nothing at all rather than something hidden.

entries.definition: affected by blight; anything that mars or prevents growth or prosperity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British in spelling and the milder half of its pair: the good has gone out of the thing, where *blighted* adds that nothing will come of it now.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The informal member, and the offhand phrasing makes the same completeness sound quick and easy rather than momentous beside *annihilated*.

entries.definition: smoothly agreeable and courteous with a degree of sophistication
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Courtesy sanded down to inoffensiveness - agreeable because nothing is left to catch on.

entries.definition: using or marked by tact in dealing with sensitive matters or people
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Credits the handling rather than the feeling - the praise is for skill that kept something sensitive from going wrong.
examples: the hostess averted a confrontation with a diplomatic change of subject

entries.definition: using or marked by tact in dealing with sensitive matters or people
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same praise in a longer, stiffer shape, where *diplomatic* carries it without the extra weight.

entries.definition: showing skill and sensitivity in dealing with people
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Makes the care visible as extreme gentleness, handling someone as though they might break, where *tactful* keeps the effort out of sight.
examples: the agency got the kid-glove treatment on Capitol Hill

entries.definition: smoothly agreeable and courteous with a degree of sophistication
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approval with calculation audible in it - the courtesy is graceful and also plainly chosen, where *tactful* sounds felt.
examples: he was too politic to quarrel with so important a personage

entries.definition: smoothly agreeable and courteous with a degree of sophistication
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The polish is the whole of it - agreeable with so little friction that you start looking for what is underneath.
examples: the manager pacified the customer with a smooth apology for the error

entries.definition: smoothly agreeable and courteous with a degree of sophistication
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Puts the sophistication out front so the courtesy reads as elegance, where *smooth* makes it read as technique.

entries.definition: showing skill and sensitivity in dealing with people
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warm where *politic* is shrewd - the skill is credited to sensitivity toward the person rather than to judgement about the situation.
examples: a tactful way of correcting someone

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal and solemn — the duty is owned and honoured rather than enforced, where *compulsory* has a rule pressing from outside.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Lets the force show: the point is that you are made to, not merely that a rule exists, which is all *required* settles for.
examples: in most schools physical education is compulsory

entries.definition: required by etiquette or usage or fashion
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Mannered, and the binding is social only — taste and custom hold it up, with nothing of the rule that stands behind *mandatory*.
examples: instruction as to when and where a silk hat is de rigueur

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the source in view — an authority has laid this down — where *required* leaves the hand that requires unnamed.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and weighty, fastening the obligation onto whoever it rests upon instead of stating it as a general rule the way *mandatory* does.
examples: it is incumbent on me to attend

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Shuts off escape: no exception or excuse gets you out of it, where *compulsory* claims only that a rule stands behind the demand.
examples: the routine but indispensable ceremonies of state

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat and impersonal — the rule simply states itself, with none of the pressure *compulsory* puts on the person obeying.

entries.definition: morally or legally constraining or binding
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The family's plain statement that something binds, holding the moral and the legal together without saying which one is doing the work.

entries.definition: required as a prior condition or course of study
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely positional — it orders things, marking what must be satisfied first, and passes no judgement on the obligation at all.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plainest of these: it names the rule's demand and stops, dramatizing neither the force behind it nor the duty in it.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Enthusiasm with heat in it, steady and burning rather than merely eager, where *warm* only glows.

entries.definition: marked by active interest and enthusiasm
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Enthusiasm with appetite in it: the interest is active and reaches for more of what it likes.

entries.definition: intensely enthusiastic about or preoccupied with
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Informal, and the enthusiasm is put as a loss of one's senses - the overstatement is the compliment.

entries.definition: intensely enthusiastic about or preoccupied with
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Informal and British; it makes the preoccupation faintly comic without actually condemning it.
examples: they are dotty about each other

entries.definition: having or showing great excitement and interest
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain term for the state - it reports the excitement and interest without ruling on whether they are deserved, which is exactly what *overenthusiastic* rules on.
examples: was enthusiastic about taking ballet lessons

entries.definition: marked by ardent or zealous enthusiasm for a cause
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Enthusiasm fastened to a cause rather than a taste, so it reads as conviction and not just liking.

entries.definition: marked by ardent or zealous enthusiasm for a cause
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Carries the same cause-driven fervour as *evangelical* with the weight shifted onto pressing it outward rather than simply holding it.

entries.definition: intensely enthusiastic about or preoccupied with
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal, and the least flattering of the preoccupied words - the enthusiasm has swamped the wits and left the enthusiast looking foolish.
examples: gaga over the rock group's new album

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The enthusiasm is on the surface and radiating - warmly, unambiguously approving in a way *zealous* never is.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Informal; enthusiasm welded to dedication and straining to be put to use, keener to act than to weigh.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The one word here that passes judgement: it grants the enthusiasm and marks it as more than the occasion warranted.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The mildest way to call enthusiasm strong - felt and unmistakable, but temperate beside *ardent*.

entries.definition: intensely enthusiastic about or preoccupied with
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Enthusiasm as sheer unrestrained force, less self-mocking than *crazy* and more like something the enthusiast cannot rein in.

entries.definition: marked by active interest and enthusiasm
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same active interest as *avid*, hardened into commitment - an edge that can read as admirable drive or as too much of it.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Sleek and assured - it praises elegance that looks effortless, where *smart* praises elegance that looks attended to.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Derisive - the style is a pose being struck, so the word withholds the very compliment *chic* pays.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warm, informal approval that grants elegance outright, without the cool appraisal running under *chic*.

entries.definition: having elegance or taste or refinement in manners or dress
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Treats the elegance as a standard met rather than a judgement shown, which is what holds it a step below *stylish*.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: British, and the admiration is broad and hearty - it takes in the whole impression rather than any fineness of judgement.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Crisp, unfussy praise for trimness and polish, without the flair *chic* lays claim to.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Playful approval with the flash left in - it enjoys the show that *chic* would find excessive.

entries.definition: having elegance or taste or refinement in manners or dress
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Plain approval of taste itself - the elegance is credited to the person's own eye rather than to anything they have matched.
examples: a little less posh but every bit as stylish as Lord Peter Wimsey

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Informal and breezy - admiration blurted rather than weighed, lighter on its feet than *classy*.
examples: a swish pastry shop on the Rue du Bac

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approval held slightly at arm's length - the *-ish* keeps it from committing the way *chic* does.

entries.definition: expressing or manifesting praise or approval
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Cooler than *approving*: the praise arrives as endorsement, stated rather than warmly felt.

entries.definition: expressing or manifesting praise or approval
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal to the point of stiffness — the same praise as *approving* lifted into an official register.

entries.definition: expressing or manifesting praise or approval
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: A near-twin of *approbative* in force, ceremonious enough that the praise reads as conferred rather than simply shown.

entries.definition: expressing or manifesting praise or approval
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain word for approval that shows — in a look, a tone or a word — where *favorable* can stay unexpressed.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The broadest approval here, covering a disposition, a sign or an outcome alike, and unlike *approving* it never requires the approval to be spoken.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The British spelling, carrying exactly the force of *favorable* and adding nothing to it.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The mildest of these — a leaning in someone's favour rather than praise of any kind, so nothing need be expressed as it must with *approving*.

entries.definition: expressing or manifesting praise or approval
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Literary and heightened, its praise closer to applause than to the bare assent of *affirmative*.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A speech word: it grades how thickly the regional colouring comes through, not how plainly a thing shows itself.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Near-instrumental in feel — it frames the thing as something a look or a test turns up, where *perceptible* frames it as something the senses take in.

entries.definition: capable of being seen or noticed
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The most guarded of the three — it grants only that the thing can be picked out, without *evident*'s suggestion that it announces itself.

entries.definition: capable of being seen or noticed
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Stronger than *discernible* on the same footing: what is evident presents itself rather than waiting to be made out.
examples: a clearly evident erasure in the manuscript

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Raises the degree rather than the ease — the thing stands out by how strongly it is set off, not by how little effort finding it takes.

entries.definition: capable or worthy of being noticed
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain, unjudged term of the set — it rates a thing as able or worth noticing without saying whether the noticing is welcome, which is exactly what *obtrusive* adds.
examples: noticeable for its vivid historical background

entries.definition: capable of being seen or noticed
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The flattest of the three — a bare statement that observation is possible, carrying none of *evident*'s force.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The one member that judges: it puts the noticing at the top of the scale and calls it unwanted, where *marked* only measures how far the scale runs.
examples: the obtrusive behavior of a spoiled child

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Pitches the same easy visibility at the observer's senses rather than at a search, which is what sets it apart from *detectable*.
examples: he continued after a perceptible pause

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Carries the same heightened degree as *marked*, but with the sense of a quality pushed forward until it cannot be missed.

entries.definition: capable of arousing and holding the attention
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The hold is inward and quiet, attention drawn in rather than seized as by *gripping*.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warm and easy - the praise is for the pleasure given, not for any grip on attention of the kind *gripping* asserts.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The stiffer, more formal shape beside *amusing*, claiming the same pleasure with less warmth in the saying.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Understated praise - the enjoyment is framed as a pleasant turning-aside, milder than *amusing*.

entries.definition: capable of arousing and holding the attention
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Stronger than *absorbing*: attention is not merely drawn in but wholly occupied, with nothing left over.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Light approval - it promises agreeable diversion rather than the deep hold *engrossing* claims.

entries.definition: capable of arousing and holding the attention
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The hold works like a spell - attention is charmed into staying rather than pinned there as by *riveting*.

entries.definition: capable of arousing and holding the attention
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Physical in its force - attention is taken hold of rather than invited, where *fascinating* wins it.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The flattest word here - it grants that attention is held and says nothing about how hard, which *absorbing* and *riveting* both do.

entries.definition: capable of arousing interest or curiosity
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The pull is curiosity rather than pleasure - it promises something not yet given, where *fascinating* holds you with what it shows.
examples: our team came up with some most intriguing finds

entries.definition: sufficiently interesting to be reported in a newspaper
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A threshold rather than a compliment - it measures whether interest clears the bar for reporting, where the rest of the family reports the pull itself.

entries.definition: capable of arousing and holding the attention
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The most immobilising of these - attention is fixed in place, not merely drawn in as by *absorbing*.

entries.definition: no longer in your possession or control; unable to be found or recovered
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flat, final member - it puts a thing beyond holding and beyond recovery both, naming a deprivation rather than a mishap.

entries.definition: lost temporarily; as especially put in an unaccustomed or forgotten place
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Gentlest here - the thing is still somewhere, merely not where it was put, so the loss is provisional and faintly self-excusing.
examples: the mislaid hat turned up eventually

entries.definition: lost temporarily; as especially put in an unaccustomed or forgotten place
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The same provisional loss as *mislaid* in a flatter, more formal register, faulting the position a thing ended up in rather than the act of setting it down.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Pure report of absence - it says only that the thing cannot be found, and unlike *lost* leaves recovery open.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The condemning member - what was had was spent to no purpose, and the word insists someone did the spending.

entries.definition: (of an animal) having no home or having wandered away from home
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Of an animal, it makes homelessness a settled condition rather than an incident, carrying pity and a touch of nuisance at once.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Names only the predicament of being unable to find your way - a passing disorientation beside the standing state *stray* describes, with no blame in it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Registers value come to nothing without fixing on a culprit, which is the accusation *squandered* adds.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A deflating verdict rather than a scornful one, saying only that nothing of weight is there and leaving the sneer to *vacuous*.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The outward form is intact and the inside is not, so it carries a ring of sham that flat *empty* does not.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A cool dismissal of what a thing stands for rather than of its size or loudness, drier and less final than *nonsensical*.

entries.definition: having no meaning or direction or purpose
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Plain on the surface and bleak underneath, since it withholds direction and purpose along with sense, condemning where *nonmeaningful* only records.

entries.definition: lacking the thinking capacity characteristic of a conscious being
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Descriptive rather than damning in this sense, stating an absence of thinking capacity without laying blame, where *nonsensical* passes judgement on what was produced.
examples: the shrieking of the mindless wind

entries.definition: having no meaning or direction or purpose
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Colourless and technical, it notes the absence and adds no dismay to it, where *meaningless* sounds the loss.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blunt and unadorned, refusing the thing any intelligible sense without softening the refusal.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The fuller, more formal judgement that nothing can be made of the thing at all, weightier in the mouth than blunt *nonsense*.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plainest statement in the family, that meaning is simply absent, with none of the scorn *vacuous* or *nonsensical* carry.
examples: Silence is better than unmeaning words

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The withering member of the three: formal, and it treats the missing force as a fault rather than a fact.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the deliberation and no more — the effect was composed, which is a fact before it is a complaint.

entries.definition: contrived by art rather than nature
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The family's flat baseline: it says a thing was contrived rather than grown and stops there, where *unreal* goes on to deny it.

entries.definition: having particular physiological functions augmented or replaced by electronic or electromechanical components
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Strictly technical — it reports function augmented or replaced by machinery and carries none of the deficiency the rest of the family hangs on the made.

entries.definition: (used of color) artificially produced; not natural
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Colour got by stripping rather than adding, and the word keeps the drained, washed-out feel of that.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Withering — the thing is flat, propped up, and has nothing behind it.

entries.definition: artificial as if portrayed in a film
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Gives the thing the sheen of a screen image and the same nothing behind the surface.
examples: a novel with flat celluloid characters

entries.definition: (used of color) artificially produced; not natural
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The blankest of these — the colour was put there, with no hint of how or how deep.

entries.definition: (used of color) artificially produced; not natural
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The British spelling, identical in force to *colored*: applied colour, stated without comment.

entries.definition: using artistic forms and conventions to create effects; not natural or spontaneous
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The British spelling, carrying exactly the measured, analytic weight of *conventionalized*.

entries.definition: using artistic forms and conventions to create effects; not natural or spontaneous
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Says the form was settled by convention rather than felt in the moment — cool and analytic, a shortfall of spontaneity rather than of substance.

entries.definition: (used of color) artificially produced; not natural
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Puts the colour in deep rather than on the surface, more concrete than *colored* and no harsher for it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Makes that arrangement a performance put on for an onlooker, so what looked spontaneous reads as put-up — the accusation *arranged* stops short of.
examples: one of those artfully staged photographs

entries.definition: using artistic forms and conventions to create effects; not natural or spontaneous
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The one here that can name a deliberate artistic manner rather than a failure, where *unlifelike* is only a falling short.
examples: a stylized mode of theater production

entries.definition: artificial as if portrayed in a film
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Manufactured-feeling rather than lived — the same screen-thin unreality as *celluloid*, without the sheen.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A plain report of the shortfall, measuring the thing against life and finding it thin, with none of *cardboard*'s contempt.

entries.definition: contrived by art rather than nature
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Denies the thing any standing in reality at all, where *artificial* only reports how it came to be.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the fault on the surface - a mark on something otherwise sound, where *flawed* lets the fault run through it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Grades speech or writing as falling short of fluent - a shortfall in the language itself, not *defective*'s fault built into a thing.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Says errors and alterations have got in, so the thing can no longer be trusted as it stands - heavier than *flawed*, which admits a fault without unsettling the whole.
examples: spoke a corrupted version of the language

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The participle points back at a sound original that errors have since entered, where *corrupt* simply reports the state.
examples: spoke a corrupted version of the language

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the defect as a verdict on the whole item - colder and more final than *faulty*.
examples: I returned the appliance because it was defective

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Workaday and remediable - it locates a fault to be put right rather than writing the thing off the way *defective* does.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same defect read as structural rather than a spot, which is why it lands harder than *blemished*.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain word for falling short of perfect - it states the shortfall and stops there, without *defective*'s implication that something inside has gone wrong.
examples: had only an imperfect understanding of his responsibilities

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely a statement of capacity - it says imperfection could be introduced and passes no judgement, where *defective* and *corrupt* both condemn.

entries.definition: failing to meet a standard of manufacture due to an imperfection
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Grades an item as missing the standard of manufacture, registering the imperfection while cushioning it - far short of calling it *defective*.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blunt and total - it leaves the notion nothing salvageable, where *impractical* leaves it merely unworkable.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Contemptuous - it casts the unsoundness as thinking abandoned before it was finished, faulting the effort as much as the result.

entries.definition: not practical; not workable or not given to practical matters
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain term of the family - it states the unworkability and stops there, without the ridicule *crazy* and *half-baked* carry.
examples: refloating the ship proved impractical because of the expense
he is intelligent but too impractical for commercial work

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The barest of these spellings, and the shortness suits a word that makes no argument, only a verdict.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A variant spelling of *meshugge* and no gentler for it - the same unadorned charge of senselessness.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Colloquial and flat - it calls the thing senseless outright, with none of the picture-making *half-baked* offers.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The extra syllables give it a flourish the shorter spellings lack, but the judgement of senselessness is unchanged.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Another form of the same dismissal - senselessness stated as settled fact, where *quixotic* would at least credit an aim.

entries.definition: not sensible about practical matters; idealistic and unrealistic
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Faults the want of practical sense while crediting the ideals behind it, so the disapproval comes out half-admiring.
examples: as quixotic as a restoration of medieval knighthood

entries.definition: not sensible about practical matters; idealistic and unrealistic
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The gentlest of these - the unrealism is charged to an idealizing temperament rather than a defect, and can be said almost fondly.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Flippant - the foolishness is treated as entertaining eccentricity, so it stings less than *crazy* at the same verdict.
examples: a screwball proposal without a prayer of working

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Insulting in a way the others are not - it puts the unsoundness down to a mind too soft to hold a firm thought.

entries.definition: not related to or suitable for everyday needs or activities
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Carries no verdict at all - it records unsuitability for everyday needs where *impractical* implies a fault.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Locates the trouble in the handling rather than in anyone's judgement, so a thoroughly sensible thing can still earn it.

entries.definition: not sensible about practical matters; idealistic and unrealistic
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts a look of fanaticism on the same unrealism, so where *romantic* indulges it this one warns against it.
examples: a wild-eyed dream of a world state

entries.definition: (of plants) bearing or characterized by aments or catkins
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Places a plant by the catkins that characterize it, as flatly as *amentiferous* and with as little praise in it.

entries.definition: (of plants) bearing or characterized by aments or catkins
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Technical and classifying: it records that the plant carries catkins and offers no verdict at all on how much it yields.

entries.definition: (of farmland) capable of being farmed productively
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: A settled favourable verdict on land, but only that it could be farmed well - potential where *rich* asserts the yield itself.

entries.definition: (of farmland) capable of being farmed productively
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: States the same promise as *arable* transparently through the act of cultivating, so it reads as an open possibility rather than a standing classification of the land.

entries.definition: (of farmland) capable of being farmed productively
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Heavier and more literal than *cultivable*, claiming no more than that the work of cultivation can be done here.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Elevated praise for a mind that generates abundantly, richer and more admiring than a flat *productive*.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises a mind as ground ideas grow from - readiness and promise, where *prolific* counts what has actually come out of it.

entries.definition: of animals having fur (especially of commercial quality)
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Coolly appraising rather than approving - it marks an animal as carrying fur worth having, without any compliment to the animal.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A bare compound naming what the plant puts out, with none of the claim about quantity that *productive* carries.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Says only that oil is present inside - containing rather than yielding, so nothing is being produced here at all.

entries.definition: producing or capable of producing (especially abundantly)
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Plain approval of output that covers both actual yield and the bare capacity for it, where *prolific* insists the yield is already there.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Admiration measured by sheer quantity of intellectual output, where *fecund* admires its richness instead.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Short, everyday and emphatic, asserting abundance outright where *productive* still allows mere capacity.

entries.definition: (of farmland) capable of being farmed productively
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The most physical of the land words, tying the ground's promise to the labour of tilling it where *arable* keeps the judgement abstract.

entries.definition: not adhering to ethical or moral principles
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Contemptuous - it ranks the character as low, not merely at fault, where *immoral* records the failure and leaves the person's standing alone.
examples: a base, degrading way of life

entries.definition: bringing or deserving severe rebuke or censure
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: States the desert rather than colouring it - the thing has earned rebuke, and the word says so and stops.

entries.definition: bringing or deserving severe rebuke or censure
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the weight of a legal charge behind a censure that is moral rather than legal, which makes it an outcry where *condemnable* is a ruling.

entries.definition: bringing or deserving severe rebuke or censure
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Voices the disapproval as dismay - the thing is bad enough to be lamented, not merely bad enough to be rebuked.

entries.definition: not adhering to ethical or moral principles
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flat categorical charge: measured against a standard and found outside it, with the force sitting in the standard rather than in the tone.

entries.definition: wrong in e.g. opinion or judgment
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Faults the judgment while leaving the intention unblamed - being led wrong is a softer charge than being wrong.

entries.definition: wrong in e.g. opinion or judgment
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Records the error and nothing else, no reproach attaching, where *misguided* still suggests the opinion was badly arrived at.

entries.definition: bringing or deserving severe rebuke or censure
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and judicial in weight, handing the blame down as a finding rather than an outburst - the cold end of *criminal*.
examples: adultery is as reprehensible for a husband as for a wife

entries.definition: bringing or deserving severe rebuke or censure
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the fault in the thing itself rather than in the verdict on it, imputing wickedness where *reprehensible* only assigns blame.

entries.definition: contrary to conscience or morality or law
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The family's flat verdict, condemning without heat and reaching conscience, morality and law with the same single word.
examples: it is wrong for the rich to take advantage of the poor

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The danger sits in the picture rather than in any verdict - a pace fast enough to break a neck, which can sound thrilling as readily as reckless.

entries.definition: of uncertain outcome; especially fraught with risk
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The bare formation, saying only that an outcome is full of chance, without the wariness *chancy* packs into the same idea.

entries.definition: of uncertain outcome; especially fraught with risk
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and shrugging - the outcome is handed to luck, which is enough to mark the thing as not worth counting on.

entries.definition: involving or causing danger or risk; liable to hurt or harm
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat and unarguable - it states that harm can follow and leaves the judging to someone else, where *unsafe* already faults the thing.

entries.definition: (of persons) dangerously reckless or violent as from urgency or despair
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Aimed at a person rather than a situation - past caution and liable to violence, and the despair behind it does nothing to soften the warning.

entries.definition: of uncertain outcome; especially fraught with risk
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal, with a gambler's wince in it - the odds are being felt rather than merely noted.
examples: an extremely dicey future on a brave new world of liquid nitrogen, tar, and smog

entries.definition: of uncertain outcome; especially fraught with risk
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British and dismissive - the thing is not just uncertain but not to be relied on, the most distrustful way of putting the same risk.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and classifying - it registers danger as a property to be assessed, cooler than *risky*, which sounds like advice.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Condemns outright, because here the danger is designed - something is laying a trap, and the word says so.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and dry for something with teeth - it charges a creature with the habit of biting, not merely a single bite.
examples: they deliberately gave me a skittish and mordacious mount

entries.definition: caught in a difficult or dangerous situation
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Informal, and the image does the work: the danger is a trap someone is caught in rather than a failing of theirs.
examples: there I was back on the hook

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Heightened and declamatory - it announces danger with a flourish that *perilous* manages without.
examples: a parlous journey on stormy seas

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Grave and unironic - danger at full weight, more formal than *dangerous* and with none of the hedging in *chancy*.
examples: a perilous voyage across the Atlantic in a small boat

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Everyday and weighing - it frames the danger as something one might knowingly take on, where *hazardous* only labels it.
examples: extremely risky going out in the tide and fog

entries.definition: involving or causing danger or risk; liable to hurt or harm
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Measures the thing against a standard of safety it fails, so the danger arrives with a fault attached that *dangerous* leaves off.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Relishes the danger instead of warning against it, giving the same risk a heat that *hazardous* keeps out.

entries.definition: sharply contrasted in character or purpose
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Casts the unlikeness as a matched opposition, two things defined against each other rather than merely unalike as in *different*.
examples: practices entirely antithetical to her professed beliefs

entries.definition: sharply contrasted in character or purpose
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The fuller and weightier-sounding form beside *antithetic*, carrying the same sense of two things set squarely against each other.
examples: practices entirely antithetical to her professed beliefs

entries.definition: of many different kinds purposefully arranged but lacking any uniformity
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Turns difference into a made mixture — the variety is arranged, though nothing in it matches.

entries.definition: very opposed in nature or character or purpose
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Marks unlikeness strong enough to amount to opposition, past the plain difference of *different* but short of the total inversion of *diametric*.
examples: acts contrary to our code of ethics
the facts point to a contrary conclusion

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Makes the difference visible — the unlikeness is what strikes you when the two are set side by side.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Frames that same striking unlikeness as a property a thing has rather than an effect it produces, the more analytic-sounding of the pair with *contrasting*.

entries.definition: characterized by opposite extremes; completely opposed
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Puts the two at opposite ends of a single line, so the difference is total rather than merely sharp as in *contrasting*.
examples: in diametric contradiction to his claims

entries.definition: characterized by opposite extremes; completely opposed
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The extended form of *diametric*, identical in force and a shade more formal in shape.

entries.definition: unlike in nature or quality or form or degree
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The bare statement of unlikeness, fixing no degree — it says two things are not the same and stops there.
examples: took different approaches to the problem
on different sides of the issue
this meeting was different from the earlier one

entries.definition: fundamentally different or distinct in quality or kind
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Places the unlikeness at the root — a difference of kind rather than of degree, deeper than the surface difference of *different*.
examples: such disparate attractions as grand opera and game fishing

entries.definition: (often followed by ‘from’) not alike; different in nature or quality
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: States the unlikeness as a clean separation of one thing from another, without any of the extremity of *diametric*.
examples: the word ‘nationalism’ is used in at least two distinct senses
a tree related to but quite distinct from the European beech
management had interests quite distinct from those of their employees

entries.definition: (often followed by ‘from’) not alike; different in nature or quality
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Puts the same unlikeness in terms of what can be told apart, so the difference is one that survives inspection, where *distinct* just asserts it.

entries.definition: diverging from another or from a standard
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Makes the difference a moving apart rather than a settled state, and lets a standard be the thing departed from, where *disparate* simply finds two things unlike.

entries.definition: characterized by opposite extremes; completely opposed
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plainest way to state complete opposition, where *diametric* and *polar* dress the same total reversal in a figure.

entries.definition: characterized by opposite extremes; completely opposed
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Renders the opposition as two extremes with nothing between them, giving the contrast a fixed maximum that *contrary* leaves open-ended.

entries.definition: of many different kinds purposefully arranged but lacking any uniformity
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Spreads the same idea across the kinds themselves, a plural of difference, where *assorted* keeps attention on the mixing.
examples: his disguises are many and various
various experiments have failed to disprove the theory
cited various reasons for his behavior

entries.definition: sufficiently significant to affect the whole world
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Trades gravity for reach — the effect is felt across the whole world, and the word keeps the physical jolt of its image.

entries.definition: highly significant or important especially bringing about or marking the beginning of a new development or era
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The active twin of *epochal* — it credits the thing with making the new beginning rather than merely marking it.

entries.definition: highly significant or important especially bringing about or marking the beginning of a new development or era
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Adds a boundary to the weight: not just great effect but the opening of something new, which *momentous* never requires.
examples: epochal decisions made by Roosevelt and Churchill

entries.definition: serving as or based on evidence
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Carries no appraisal at all — it marks only that something rests on or supplies evidence, so it sits outside any scale of weight.
examples: evidential signs of a forced entry

entries.definition: serving as or based on evidence
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The stiffer, more formal twin of *evidential*, and just as free of praise or blame.

entries.definition: far-reaching and thoroughgoing in effect especially on the nature of something
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Points downward rather than upward: the effect reaches what a thing is, describing depth of change instead of how much it is admired.
examples: the fundamental revolution in human values that has occurred
committed the fundamental error of confusing spending with extravagance

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: More insistent than *significant* — it claims the thing matters and should be treated accordingly, not merely that it registers.

entries.definition: fairly large or important in effect; influential
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Deliberately unemphatic — it grants real effect and influence while stopping far short of *monumental*.
examples: played a large role in the negotiations

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Lifts *significant* to a height where the weight itself is the point, grave and admiring at once.
examples: deciding to drop the atom bomb was a very momentous decision

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Makes the significance imposing, something that stands over whatever is beside it, where *noteworthy* only asks you to look.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: A modest claim: it asks for attention and promises nothing beyond it.
examples: a noteworthy fact is that her students rarely complain
a noteworthy advance in cancer research

entries.definition: far-reaching and thoroughgoing in effect especially on the nature of something
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Where *fundamental* is structural this one is grave, reaching the same way into a thing's nature but spoken with awe.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Stronger than *noteworthy* on the same ground — attention is compelled rather than merely deserved, and admiration comes with it.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A flat measure of weight in effect or meaning, asserting that something counts without saying the counting is welcome.
examples: a significant change in tax laws
a significant change in the Constitution

entries.definition: sufficiently significant to affect the whole world
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same global reach as *earthshaking*, with the world named outright instead of shaken underfoot.
examples: the contest was no world-shaking affair

entries.definition: sufficiently significant to affect the whole world
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The most violent of the three: the world does not shake but breaks, so the significance arrives as rupture.
examples: the conversation … could hardly be called world-shattering

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Informal and exuberant - a hit rather than a result, success that arrives with applause attached.
examples: for years he was a boffo box office certainty

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Profit heard as noise, busy enough to be audible, where *flourishing* keeps its liveliness quiet.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Swelling growth caught mid-expansion, promising more where *prosperous* implies arrival.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Liveliness figured as healthy growth, organic where *booming* is loud.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely positional - it records that the office is held and passes no judgement on the holding.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Blunt finality: the success is banked and out of doubt, unlike *sure-fire*, which is confident about what has yet to happen.
examples: now I am a made man forever

entries.definition: of a game (or the pitching) in which a pitcher allows the opponent no hits
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A technical description of what the pitching allowed, recording the fact where the rest of the family evaluates.
examples: The visiting pitcher no-hit the home team today
The home team no-hit the visiting team last week

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Ornate and faintly grand, giving profitable liveliness a costume that *thriving* does without.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Measured, almost accounting approval - results were yielded, with none of *boffo*'s noise about them.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The participle keeps the gain in motion - still climbing, where *prosperous* names a state already reached.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Settled rather than surging: comfortable profit as a condition, not a rush.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The loudest word in the set - profit at full volume, and it refuses to be understated.

entries.definition: having achieved success or recognition by your own efforts
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approval aimed at the person rather than the outcome, crediting the effort behind the success.

entries.definition: having succeeded or being marked by a favorable outcome
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The family's flat statement that the outcome went well, carrying none of the swagger *boffo* brings to the same result.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Confidence issued in advance, guaranteeing a success that *made* can already report as done.
examples: a sure-fire way to get rich

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Vitality as the measure of profit, doing well the way a living thing does and with none of *roaring*'s noise.
examples: did a thriving business in orchids

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Smartness with a sharp edge to it - the neatness reads as definition of outline, where *trim* praises proportion.
examples: a clean-cut and well-bred young man

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain word of approval for it - nothing out of place, where *orderly* wants an arrangement behind the tidiness.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Credits the system rather than the surface: things are arranged, not merely unmessy as with *neat*.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: A quiet yes to tidiness with no appraisal in it, next to the brisk verdict of *shipshape*.

entries.definition: characterized by order and neatness; free from disorder
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The briskest approval in the family - order thorough enough that nothing is left to put right, where *neat* is satisfied with the surface.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Informal, and the tidiness is put on rather than native - a spruced state, where *well-kept* implies it never lapsed.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The bare arrangement word - things put right, with none of the polish *shipshape* claims.

entries.definition: marked by order and cleanliness in appearance or habits
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Mild, unemphatic approval that takes in habits as well as appearance, where *clean-cut* is a verdict on looks alone.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Spruce and compact - the same smartness pulled tight, without *clean-cut*'s sharpness of line.
examples: the trig corporal in his jaunty cap

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Here the smartness is one of proportion, nothing loose and nothing spare, where *clean-cut* is about crispness.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approves by subtraction, the merit lying in what is gone, where *neat* and *orderly* credit an arrangement.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flatter than *uncluttered* - it denies mess rather than paying a compliment for its absence.
examples: the unlittered shoulders of the road

entries.definition: characterized by order and neatness; free from disorder
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises the keeping as much as the state - the order reads as sustained, where *shipshape* praises how complete it is.

entries.definition: not defended or capable of being defended
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and analytic, looking from the attacker's side at what can be gone after, where *undefended* only reports what is not there.

entries.definition: vulnerable to danger especially of discredit or suspicion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The one member whose danger is to standing rather than to body - exposure that invites suspicion and discredit.
examples: she found herself in a compromising situation

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British spelling, identical in force: helplessness rather than the neutral gap *undefended* reports.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Pitying - the subject is helpless and unsupplied, where *undefended* notes only the absence.

entries.definition: (of flora or fauna) in imminent danger of extinction
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A graded status term rather than a verdict, and the severe end of that grading - extinction imminent, not merely likely.

entries.definition: not able to be protected against attack
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Absolute here: no protection could hold, a harder claim than *undefended*'s report that none is in place.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Treats the exposure as a standing property of the thing's condition, an adverse mark rather than a neutral gap.

entries.definition: not defended or capable of being defended
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The mildest wording for the same state, naming the gap as a plain fact of position rather than the failure *undefendable* implies.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely a property of the barrier - it says what can be got through, with no suggestion that anything is coming through.

entries.definition: (of flora or fauna) likely in the near future to become endangered
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The graded step below *endangered*: likelihood of peril soon rather than peril arrived.
examples: the spotted owl is a threatened species, not yet an endangered one

entries.definition: not defended or capable of being defended
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Puts the weight on impossibility - not that defences are absent but that none could be made to hold.

entries.definition: not defended or capable of being defended
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Bare report of an absence, with no claim that defence was tried or that it could have worked.

entries.definition: subjected to enemy attack or censure
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Shifts from susceptibility to fact - the blows are landing, and they can be censure as readily as weapons.

entries.definition: subjected to enemy attack or censure
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The vivid twin of *under attack*, its gunfire image carrying the same double reach over assault and criticism.
examples: an official under fire for mismanagement

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The blunt everyday form of the same adverse judgement, stating the danger without locating the weakness as *insecure* does.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The family's flat baseline: it registers that an attack could land without saying anything is missing or anyone is at fault.
